22/Jul/26 7:47 PM;5f3432cde115420046434665;[~accountid:712020:f9a894b1-f824-4a33-a40d-1d507fe78d86] translating specific inks to Names and to RGB (web) colors is always a bit of science mixed with a bit of art mixed with a bit of hocus pocus.

These “greenish” colors are being reported as Black because they have low HSL brightness. With this low brightness, the hue is never being considered. 

So I’ve changed this to consider “Saturation” as well, based on some suggestions from Claude. With that in place, the file in question would have reported 1 instance of White and three instances of a very-similar-but-technically-different “Cyan.” 

“Why not green?” you ask?

{quote}At ~161°, your color falls into the 135–195 range, which is mapped to "Cyan". That is technically correct in HSL terms — (0, 71, 49) is a dark blue-green/teal, which sits closer to cyan than pure green on the color wheel (pure green is 120°).{quote}

This is on DEV for review. Note that while I reprocessed this one icon to show the before/after differences, other icons would not be reprocessed without intervention or a future update to the icon file.

Also Obsoletion is a non reversible operation, so we shouldn’t be able to change that state via button, bulk update, or any other way. (Other then maybe Dev or Devine intervention)

As indicated in the UI changes explained in [https://jira-pg.atlassian.net/browse/CPM-369|https://jira-pg.atlassian.net/browse/CPM-369|smart-link], we need to be able to assign OUs and Regions to Families, and that data must flow to Enovia.

We can use 1 new field to send that information (FamilyAttributes) and have them be sent like Fabric Care, EUROPE ENTERPRISE; Oral Care, EUROPE ENTERPRISE. → *To validate with Tripo/Jyoti how this data must flow.*



[~accountid:5f3432cde115420046434665] to provide some icon output json (update to enovia) so that we can modify it to expectations.



*One Icon can be rep for only one family.*

*Current assumption:* Both Icons, and Families, can have multiple OUs assigned, but when it comes to Regions, they will either be single region, or be global (all existing regions assigned). This will be controlled by the process, by letting the icon-uploader team and the OUs to not use multi region icons unless they’re global.

The reason why we need this logic is to allow the following scenarios:

*BC1 (Case 1)*

I have a FC NA icon, version 1, released.

*BC1-CM1 (Case 1, Scenario 1)*

If I add it to a family (FamilyName1) that is assigned to FC NA, the icon will be up versioned to version 2, and released immediately (without approval process). When doing so, the newer version is part of a family, but is not family rep, so we don’t send update to Enovia about v2, but we’ll send them update about v1 being obsoleted (and set validity date to yesterday).

*BC2-CM2*

If I add it to a family (FamilyName1) that is assigned to FC NA, and the icon is set as REP to that family, the icon will be up versioned to version 2, and released immediately (without approval process). When doing so, because Icon is rep, we send update to Enovia about v2 being released, and also about v1 being obsolete (and set validity date to yesterday).



*BC2*

I have an icon that is assigned to both FC NA and OC NA.

*BC2-CM1*

I’m adding this Icon to a family that is assigned to FC NA (FamilyName1). Since this icon is not a rep for that family, Enovia doesn’t need to create a clone for FC NA of that icon, as they will just use the Rep for that. However, they need to have a standalone icon for OC NA. To allow that, we will use subtraction logic.

Icon: FC NA, OC NA, not REP of FamilyName1.

FamilyName1: FC NA

Icon_data_sent_to_enovia: OC NA (hiding FC NA, and family name)

*BC2-CM2*

I’m adding this icon to FamilyName1 (owned by FC NA), but i’m also setting it as the Rep for that family.

Enovia will need a clone for FC NA that is rep, a clone for OC NA that is not part of family. They will apply that logic on their end. We’ll just give them the full information of the icon, and they will use the attributes in the family to determine which clones they need to create or not.

Still obsoleting version 1, and setting validity date to yesterday.



*BC3*

I have an icon that is assigned to OC NA and FC NA, part of FamilyName1  (owned by FC NA) so Enovia only sees the data for OC NA (and no family assigned) as Icon is not the rep of FamilyName1.

*BC3-CM1*

If I assign the icon as Family Rep for FamilyName1, I’ll obsolete version 1, release version 2 as rep, and send both the data for OC NA, FC NA, and family to Enovia. _They will need to make sure on their end that the OC NA clone is not part of a family, but the FC NA clone is._

*BC3-CM2*

If I also assign the icon to FamilyName2 (owned by OC NA), by the subtraction logic, Enovia no longer sees the icon, as it’s only available for FC NA and OC NA, and for both OUs the icon is in a family, but is not a rep for any of the families.

This means that we must obsolete the existing v1, create and release v2, but v2 won’t be sent to Enovia, as they will use the Reps of those 2 families.

*BC3-CM3*

If I remove the icon from FamilyName1, I will obsolete it and change validity date, and release v2, with all the data assigned to it as it’s no longer part of any family.



*BC4*

Icon is FC NA, OC NA, and is rep of FamilyName1 (owned by FC NA).

*BC4-CM1*

I remove it as a rep

*BC4-CM2*

I remove it from the family

*BC5*

Icon in 2 families, not rep

*BC5-CM1*

I move icon from one of the families to another family.

*BC6*

Icon in 2 families, Rep of Both → Not possible

*BC7*

Icon in 2 families, Rep of One,

*BC7-CM1*

Changing one of families, that icon is not rep of.

*BC8*

Icon is in 1 family, owned by both OUs (FC NA, OC NA)

*BC8-CM1*

We modify family to remove 1 OU

*BC9*

Icon in 2 OU, Family Rep in FamilyName1 (Owned by FC NA)

*BC9-CM1*

We modify family to remove 1 OU

*BC10*

Icon is in family owned by 1 OU

*BC10-CM1*

column1: Create new version with same graphic
column30:
When we create a new version, we are forced to upload a new graphic (or reupload the same one). 

*New version should be created without requesting new icon, but new icon can be provided.* 

If it’s not provided, reuse the graphic of the previous version.

2 Scenarios:

# If *new version is created without uploading new graphic*, the canonical and graphic *ID will stay the same, but the version will increase by 1.*
# If *new version is created by also uploading a new graphic*, the canonical ID stays the same, *the graphic ID changes, and the version will increate by 1.*
column1576:
27/May/26 5:33 AM;5f3432cde115420046434665;[~accountid:712020:f9a894b1-f824-4a33-a40d-1d507fe78d86] I suspect there is a bit of misunderstanding as to what these various “IDs” represent.

# The Canonical ID is the authoritative Id shared by the entire “lineage” of an icon from version 1 through version N.  It does not change.
# The Unique Graphic Id represents a version of an Icon. The version represented by an asset with a given Unique Graphic Id contains all the unique metadata about that version. A new Unique Graphic Id is generated with each version – it is the incrementing database primary key for that row.

So keeping the Unique Graphic Id the same across different versions is probably not going to be an easy task without inventing new Id-like structures.

There is one other Id which is not displayed in the UI anywhere: the {{AssetFileId}}. This is the Id of the actual binary asset (generally a PDF) which is associated with a version of an Icon. _(It can be shared by completely different Icons, technically, but that is pretty unusual.)_

So…

# We could allow a new version to reuse the same icon as the previous version, but keep displaying the newly-generated Unique Graphic Id as before.
# We could allow a new version to reuse the same icon as the previous version, but we could change what we currently display in the Unique Graphic Id spot to, instead, be the AssetFileId.  

#1 is simplest and likely has the fewest risks. It is also closest to what is probably _already happening today…_ You make a New Version, upload the same PDF again, and the system is already hashing, comparing, and throwing out the duplicate. 03/Jun/26 10:45 PM;5f3432cde115420046434665;[~accountid:712020:f9a894b1-f824-4a33-a40d-1d507fe78d86] we should probably talk this through. 

The duplicate checking algo is currently using pHash. (Other options are dHash and aHash, but for the most part, they are similar.)  This is not a firm determination of an exact match. It’s an approximate calculation of how “close” one images is to another. If it is within a certain threshold of “closeness,” we can guess that it *_might_* be a duplicate of an existing icon. But we cannot tell that FOR SURE using this algorithm.

On DEV right now is one approach to this. 

!image-20260603-203442.png|width=1159,alt="image-20260603-203442.png"!

The user is *encouraged, but not required,* to review existing “close matches” to decide if they should continue uploading this icon.  

Originally, we hard-stopped the attempt to upload an image which was a “close match.”  But if an icon has genuine-but-subtle differences, it risks getting blocked from uploading with no way to override the system.  So at present, it is an _optional_ check. We can always go back to hard-stop, but it will raise management issues down the road.

*Now, the bulk upload is an even nastier version of this issue.* There is not an elegant way to give the user any feedback on a “close match” before it is too late and the asset would have already been added to the system.  We could do a literal hash of the binary of the PDF and block *those*, but that doesn’t seem terribly useful – we already discard literal binary matches on PDFs in favor of associating them to the existing PDF. We could decide to report “close matches” on screen during the initial stage of import, but then we would need to develop some way of _doing something_ with those close matches, and that is presently out of the scope of this card.  (At one point, Rachel or maybe you had mocked up a big set of screens to deal with this, if I recall correctly.)

Thoughts on all of this?

column30:
*As a* member of the curation team,
*I want* the country field to dynamically narrow down options based on the region selected,
*So that* I can easily select the appropriate country without having to sift through irrelevant options, improving efficiency and accuracy in my work.

h3. Acceptance Criteria:

# *Region Selection*:
#* When a user selects a region from the region dropdown, the country field should automatically update to display only the countries associated with that selected region.
# *Default State*:
#* If no region is selected, the country field should show all available countries.
# *Data Integrity*:
#* The filtering logic must ensure that the relationship between regions and countries is accurately maintained, reflecting the latest data.
# *Testing*:
#* The feature should be tested across various scenarios to ensure it works correctly with multiple regions and countries.

13/Jan/26 5:42 PM;5f3432cde115420046434665;Findings based on our call…

# *“Why don’t the Regions change in IconDB when I make a change in the backend?”*
At present, there is a relatively-short-term memory cache on Regions. This is for performance reasons and because, until quite recently, Regions basically never changed. I cycled the memory on the IconDB application, and now the Regions display as intended. If Regions are expected to change more frequently in the future, we will need a cache-buster change for this.

# *“Where do the Regions in IconDB come from? Is it the same list as in Rules Manager?”*
Regions in IconDB are housed in the table *[dLabs].[Region]* which is the Canvas table for Region data.  Canvas’ list of Markets use this Region data, but a great many of those entries are set to the Region “Unknown.”

Regions in the Lookup Cluster tool for Touchless are likewise housed in the table *[dLabs].[Region]*.

Regions in Rules Manager are housed in the table *rules.PackageTriggerValue* which is the main key-value-pair table for PackageTrigger data in Rules Manager.  They have no database-managed relationship with Markets whatsoever, nor do they have a relationship with dlabs.Region.

Regions in AQIQ derive from report data submitted to AQIQ. It is stored as string data within the *[AQIQ].[tPoa]* table. It has no relationship between either the Canvas list of Regions nor the Rules Manager list of Regions.

We want to review the possibility of a Duplicate Detection interface, that should look for duplicates when uploading to IconDB. The check within the items of a bulk upload (if it’s more than 1 picture in bulk / not single upload button) and check within the IconDB database.

If potential duplicates are found in our bulk, we must select which we want to keep uploading. If none are found, it should then look for duplicates between the bulk vs Icon database. 

If potential duplicates are found between bulk vs IconDB, we must select which we want to keep uploading. If none are found, upload is successful.

Please check attached mockup.

[^IconDB bulk upload duplicate check.pptx]

Logic explained here: [https://jira-pg.atlassian.net/browse/IDB-208|https://jira-pg.atlassian.net/browse/IDB-208|smart-link]

We need a P-Hashing Algorithm to check for duplicates, within the bulk uploads done on IconDB, but also within the whole IconDB. At it’s peak, IconDB will have more than 5000 icons. Is P-Hashing feasible for this type of scaling? We are also considering on implementing an external AI model to perform the check and connect it to IconDB only to perform these checks.

Please let us know if you think P-Hashing could work for large numbers of input files, and if yes, estimate the implementation of such an algorithm.



Take into consideration that the interface (IDB-206) is not mandatory, and we might want to build this solution without a full “visual interface”. It could be enough to show the list of icon names that are considered duplicates, and ask us if we want to continue the upload or not.
